replies_after_last_own.author: parisbs
replies_after_last_own.summary:
Closing in favour of #180, which keeps the goal and changes the approach.

Two findings changed the design:

- With tool search, which Claude Code enables by default, only tool names and server instructions load at session start; a tool's description reaches the model only once the tool is loaded ([docs](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/mcp#scale-with-mcp-tool-search)). The orchestrator picks a registration before it reads any description, so the server instructions carry most of the value here.
- Generating every tool and parameter description from the configuration, as proposed above, turns fixed schemas into per-configuration factories and needs a rule for what each description says while the configuration has errors. Most of that cost exists only because the descriptions state configured values.

So #180 splits the job: descriptions describe the tool and are true under every configuration, and the server instructions are the one text generated from the configuration. The single exception is the `codex_recommend` guidance, which today overrides a configured default model; it becomes conditional so the fix works in every client.

What carries over from this thread, @naief9961-tech: one validated configuration object feeds everything the server says, two configurations are tested side by side in one process, and a misconfigured server says so instead of describing fallback values. The purpose variable is dropped to avoid new configuration surface before the 1.0 freeze (#139); the stated facts already tell registrations apart when their configuration differs. Thanks for the review.

## Current-main reproduction and accepted implementation scope

Reproduced on exact remote main 9c4382f60e2fb300c6cb877bb6ff295ecfbdf2ee, Windows amd64, Go 1.26.4, using the built public CLI and isolated HOME/USERPROFILE/ENGRAM_DATA_DIR. No user configuration or database was used.

engram doctor --json results:
- Missing ~/.gemini/config/mcp_config.json: report status ok.
- Zero-byte file: report status error with mcp_inspection_error / unexpected end of JSON input.
- Space/tab/CR/LF-only file: same inspection error.
- {}: report status ok.
All four invocations exit 0 with empty stderr; the bug concerns the JSON diagnostic status, not process failure. The reproduction harness exited 0 because it records those outcomes; it is not a claimed failing regression test.

First violated invariant: an existing config containing no JSON registrations aborts the read-only generic-adapter scan before later clients are inspected. StaleMCPCommands calls json.Unmarshal immediately after reading bytes.

Accepted design: skip zero bytes or only JSON whitespace within StaleMCPCommands, before unmarshalling. Retain all I/O and nonempty parse failures, exact setup-entry matching, and setup writer behavior. No new CLI flag or output schema.

Regression plan: public doctor tests cover missing/empty/JSON-whitespace/{}, later stale registrations, malformed nonempty JSON and non-JSON whitespace; assert config bytes and absence of newly created configs. Run focused RED/GREEN, affected Go packages, and a before/after CLI comparison. Low-risk read-only diagnostic change, no data rewrite, permission or concurrency change.
